A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MoE-Gyro and ISEBench. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark comparisons, reconstruction examples, component ablations and supplementary sensitivity experiments in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds cross-device evaluation, efficiency measurements, gate comparisons and task-specific PINN ablations.

M1.justification: The core experts, heuristic routing, attention, masking and losses remain unchanged. Section 5.4 adds an implemented pruned model with 1.85M parameters, whereas v1 discussed compression only as future work. The alternative MLP gate is tested without replacing the primary heuristic gate.

E1.justification: Section 5.3 adds evaluation on newly collected Huawei P70 and Xiaomi 14 recordings, substantially extending coverage to previously untested sensor domains. The motion-type comparisons subdivide the existing dataset; the VIO and SLAM discussions do not establish additional evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: The main ISEBench comparator roster is unchanged. Appendix D.2 newly evaluates a learned MLP gate against heuristic routing. HEROS-GAN is reused in added comparisons; MobileNetV2 and RTSNet are mentioned without being evaluated as new baselines.

E3.justification: v2 introduces an explicit iPhone-trained, cross-device evaluation without fine-tuning, motion-stratified comparisons, full-versus-pruned runtime evaluation and a learned-gate control. These substantially extend the evaluation design. The original 80/20 splits, sampling rate and benchmark metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test cross-device robustness, performance across motion types, compression tradeoffs, heuristic versus learned routing, and PINN's contribution within each motion type. The earlier component, masking, loss-weight and clipping-threshold studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The retained Allan-variance measurements characterize sensor noise rather than uncertainty in experimental estimates.

E6.justification: MoE-Gyro's reported PSNR changes from 8.19 to 8.29 in Table 1 and the MoE ablation table, without a stated protocol revision. Substantial new result blocks include cross-device PSNR of 7.95 for Xiaomi and 8.28 for Huawei, compressed/full inference times of 41/117 ms, and gate and taskwise PINN tradeoffs. Most original results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, attention and loss equations, Appendix A metrics and Appendix B energy-loss derivation are retained. Minor equation typesetting differences do not change their mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions and claims: unified self-supervised reconstruction and denoising, ISEBench, range extension from ±450 to ±1500 degrees/s, and 98.4% bias-instability reduction.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations of noise synthesis, internal versus external disturbances, routing failures and PINN's specialization-versus-robustness tradeoff. It also identifies residual noise in training targets as a performance limitation and frames deployment as navigation co-processing rather than high-frequency control. Appendix D substantially expands applicability and future-work discussion.

D1.justification: v2 adds a concrete code-repository link, cross-device resampling and unit-conversion instructions, a 2.56-second input duration, a proposed 0.5-second sliding-window step, pruning size and explicit memory units. These improve documentation, although pruning and MLP implementation details remain sparse.

R1.justification: v2 adds Revach et al.'s RTSNet reference to position the proposed future iterative-denoising direction. The existing related-work discussion and cited works otherwise remain, with some citation renumbering.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative are retained. v2 inserts generalization and efficiency subsections, expands Appendix D into five subsections, adds an FFT explanation and acknowledgements, corrects the DE name in the introduction, and updates the venue footer.

P2.justification: New Tables 2–4, 11 and 12 substantially expand the displayed evidence through device, motion, efficiency, gate and PINN comparisons. All six original figures are retained without graphical changes, while several floats move and the MoE ablation table gains explicit memory units.

improvement.justification: The cross-device tests and measured compression/runtime tradeoffs strengthen practical claims that v1 supported less directly. The gate and PINN analyses and noisy-target limitation also improve interpretation. These gains are useful but bounded: new experiments lack uncertainty estimates and detailed setup information, while embedded deployment and downstream navigation benefits remain prospective.
